first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing most directly addresses immediate loss of price-sensitive SMB accounts and has inherited evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. However, its effect on long-term qualified revenue, retention, and post-promotion customer quality is unclear, so memory_73 should be verified. Memory_86 is the strongest competing intervention because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, but its archived claim emphasizes early adoption rather than downstream revenue. Pending verification, use a guarded, targeted pricing test rather than a broad discount rollout.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the onboarding flow. The verified evidence directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and supports sustainable value: completion rose 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. Reject promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with 12% lower 30-day retention and failure at first renewal. Longer-term revenue impact beyond 30 days remains uncertain, so this should remain an experiment rather than a broad rollout.
